observation_summary: The test case fails with a NotSerializableException when attempting to serialize a FastDateFormat object. The stack trace indicates that an internal class, PaddedNumberField, is not serializable, causing the serialization process to fail.
hypothesis: The FastDateFormat class contains non-serializable internal fields (like PaddedNumberField) that are part of its state. Because these fields are not marked as transient and the class does not implement custom serialization logic to handle them, the default Java serialization mechanism fails when it encounters these non-serializable components.
prediction: The fix will involve either marking the problematic internal fields as 'transient' to exclude them from default serialization or making the internal classes implement the Serializable interface. If marked transient, the class will likely need to implement readObject/writeObject or a similar mechanism to re-initialize these fields upon deserialization.
experiment_rationale: The error message explicitly identifies the non-serializable class (PaddedNumberField) within the context of a serialization attempt. This confirms that the structural relationship between the serializable FastDateFormat and its internal components is broken.
reasoning_summary: This is a Relationship defect because the failure arises from a broken association between the serializable object (FastDateFormat) and its internal components (PaddedNumberField). The serialization contract is violated because the internal structure does not support the serialization requirements of the parent object. It is not an Algorithm/Method issue because the logic is correct, just incompatible with the serialization framework. It is not a Function/Class/Object issue because the capability exists, but the structural association is incorrectly defined.
evidence_used: FastDateFormat.mRules is not transient or serializable
Either we need to make the Rule interface Serializable, or make mRules transient and add deserializing code to kick off init().

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing class structure, the root cause is the broken relationship/contract between the serializable parent and its internal components, not a missing capability.
